depth.h2: What Skokie Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: Skokie grew from about 15,000 people in 1950 to nearly 60,000 by 1960, as families moved out of Chicago after the war. The median home here was built in 1959. When most of a town is built in the same few decades, its plumbing tends to wear out on the same schedule.

tiles.title: Postwar Sewer Lines at 60 to 80 Years
tiles.body: Sewer laterals from the 1940s, 50s and 60s were usually clay or cast iron. At this age, roots get in at the joints, cast iron scales up inside and sections crack. [Sewer rodding](/skokie/sewer-rodding) clears the line, and a [camera inspection](/skokie/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows whether it needs a [repair](/skokie/sewer-repair).

tiles.title: Low Water Pressure From Old Pipe
tiles.body: Many postwar homes were built with galvanized steel water pipe. It rusts from the inside, so water pressure drops slowly over the years and the first water of the morning can come out tinted. When one fixture after another loses pressure, it’s time to look at the [pipes](/skokie/leak-repairs), not just the faucet.

tiles.title: Heavy Rain and Basement Backups
tiles.body: In May 2020, Skokie got 7.35 inches of rain in five days, and the regional Deep Tunnel system filled to capacity. The village’s flood control system is designed to hold water on the street for up to four hours after a storm, which protects basements as long as your own line is ready. A [backflow valve](/skokie/flood-control-maintenance) or an [overhead sewer](/skokie/overhead-sewer-systems) keeps sewer water out of the basement.

tiles.title: Winter Freezes and Original Fixtures
tiles.body: Skokie winters bring long stretches below freezing. Pipes in exterior walls and crawl spaces freeze first, and a split pipe often starts leaking once it thaws. We’re on call 24/7 if a [pipe bursts](/skokie/burst-pipe-repair), and we can replace worn-out [faucets and shutoff valves](/skokie/faucet-installation-repair) while we’re there.

items.q: How much does a plumber cost in Skokie?
items.a: It depends on the job. The main factors are what’s wrong, how hard it is to reach, the parts or materials needed and the age of your plumbing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in. Give us a call and we’ll walk you through it.

items.q: My Skokie home was built in the 1950s. Is my sewer line due for replacement?
items.preview: Not necessarily. Age tells you where to look, not what you’ll find.
items.a: Not necessarily. Age tells you where to look, not what you’ll find. Many lines from that era still work fine, and others need a repair in one section. A [camera inspection](/skokie/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows the actual condition, so you only fix what’s broken.

items.q: Why is my water pressure so low?
items.preview: In older Skokie homes, the most common cause is galvanized steel water pipe that has rusted and narrowed inside.
items.a: In older Skokie homes, the most common cause is galvanized steel water pipe that has rusted and narrowed inside. A clogged aerator or a failing pressure valve can do it too. We’ll check the fixtures first, then the pipes, and explain your options.

items.q: What is sewer line drain cleaning?
items.preview: It’s cleaning the main line that carries everything from your house to the village sewer.
items.a: It’s cleaning the main line that carries everything from your house to the village sewer. We clear it with a [sewer rodding](/skokie/sewer-rodding) machine or, for heavy roots and grease, [hydro jetting](/skokie/hydro-jetting). Then we can run a camera so you see what caused the clog.

items.q: How do I protect my basement from sewer backups?
items.preview: Start with three things: a backflow valve on your sewer line, a sump pump with a battery backup if you have one, and a regular check of your sewer line for roots and debris.
items.a: Start with three things: a backflow valve on your sewer line, a sump pump with a battery backup if you have one, and a regular check of your sewer line for roots and debris. For homes with repeat backups, an overhead sewer system lifts basement wastewater above the level where backups happen.
